bullets.title: MSFT F4Q26 Preview: Azure ~40% growth expected; capex guidance key watch
bullets.body: Street consensus expects MSFT F4Q26 revenue of $87.62B (above $87.25B guidance midpoint), EPS $4.63, and Azure constant-currency growth of 40.3% with buyside expecting upside. Key investor focus is FY27 capex guidance (consensus $189.3B), Copilot penetration and monetization, and open-source AI strategy implications for cloud margins.

bullets.title: AMZN Q2 Preview: $197B revenue, $40.5B AWS expected; AI strategy overhauled
bullets.body: Street expects AMZN Q2 revenue $197.03B (midpoint of $194-199B guidance), AWS revenue $40.54B, operating income $23.56B, and EPS $1.82; options imply ~6.9% move. Separately, Amazon is reportedly overhauling its AI strategy and winding down most flagship in-house models, a meaningful strategic pivot.

bullets.title: NVDA: $5B stake in Safe Superintelligence; $50B HUT Texas DC leases; circular-finance concerns mount
bullets.body: NVDA takes $5B stake in Ilya Sutskever's Safe Superintelligence and signs ~$50B in leases for HUT's Texas data centers. However, credit spreads are spiking sharply on circular-finance concerns: NVDA and other hyperscalers are funding data center buildouts that buy their own chips, creating a potential negative feedback loop if AI ROI disappoints. MS credit analysis sees no immediate funding problem but the market is pricing elevated risk.

bullets.title: Semis broad selloff deepens: MU, AMD, STX, WDC down 4-7% premarket on KOSPI crash + China DUV fears
bullets.body: Semiconductor stocks broadly down 3-7% premarket (SOXX -3.68%): MU -6.2%, STX -7.1%, WDC/SNDK -7%, AMD -4.4%, ARM -4.1%. The dual catalyst is South Korea's KOSPI halting after a 10.8% crash (SK Hynix -14.7%, Samsung -13.4%) and fears over China's immersion DUV progress enabling sub-28nm chips via multi-patterning. Jefferies and JPM both flag the AI trade unwind is positioning/narrative-driven, not fundamental, with SOX at 15.8x 2Y forward PE (widest discount to SPX since Oct 2022).

bullets.title: META: $14B Texas 1GW data center JV with BlackRock; $12.5B debt offering priced at wider spreads
bullets.body: META and BlackRock announced a ~$14B, 1-gigawatt data center campus in El Paso, Texas, expected online by 2028. META simultaneously priced a $12.5B debt offering for data center projects at higher rates than a comparable year-ago deal, with hyperscaler CDS blowing out to record wides—raising questions about the sustainability of AI financing structures.

bullets.title: GOOGL/META/AMZN valuation compression: MS marks sector 'Attractive' at 18-21x 2027 EPS
bullets.body: Internet names fell 7% overall (META -8%, GOOGL -8%, AMZN -6%, UBER -9%) on AI capex scrutiny. Morgan Stanley notes sector now trades at AMZN 20x, GOOGL 21x, META 18x 2027 EPS—valuations down 12-25% vs TTM average—and marks the sector 'Attractive.' JPM models 25-50% ROIC for hyperscalers owning both models and infrastructure (GOOGL ~46%, AMZN/MSFT/META ~25-30%).

bullets.title: QCOM F3Q26 Preview: $9.7B revenue, DC ramp and China handset recovery in focus
bullets.body: QCOM reports F3Q26 AMC on July 29; Street expects $9,695M revenue (vs $9,700M guidance midpoint), EPS $2.24, and gross margin 55.6%. Key debates: ramp of DragonFly DC portfolio toward $15B DC revenue by 2029, China QCT android shipments expected to bottom in June quarter, and reported double-digit customer price increases starting September.

bullets.title: MA Q2 Preview: $9.08B revenue, 20 straight beat quarters; options imply ~3.8% move
bullets.body: Mastercard reports Q2 on July 30; consensus expects $9.08B revenue (+11.6% YoY), EPS $4.77, and operating margin 60.3%. MA has beaten revenue and EPS consensus for 20 consecutive quarters; stock +6.8% since April vs S&P +4.2%. Near-term options imply ~3.8% post-earnings move.

bullets.title: GLW down ~15% premarket: optical comms supply chain falls in sympathy
bullets.body: Corning beat Q2 revenue ($4.74B vs $4.63B est) and raised its Springboard Plan targets to $20B run rate by end-2026 and $40B by 2030 on AI optical/photonics demand, but the stock is down ~14.9% premarket—likely on profitability miss vs. expectations. Sympathy selling hits AAOI -6.6%, CIEN -6.6%, AXTI -6.3%, LITE, and other optical names.

bullets.title: CLS raises FY guidance; CORZ +5% on AMD 2.5GW data center deal
bullets.body: Celestica raised FY guidance with EPS $11.30 ex-items vs prior $10.15, with Citi noting FY27 sales could reach $34B+ vs Street $27B. Core Scientific (CORZ) +5% premarket after announcing a 530 MW (scalable to 2.5 GW) infrastructure partnership with AMD beginning 2027 under a 15-year agreement implying >$14B base revenue and at least 15% unlevered yield.

bullets.title: CDNS raises FY26 guidance; 85% buy-rated with 20% upside to avg $406 PT
bullets.body: Cadence beat Q2 EPS by $0.06, raised FY26 EPS guidance $0.16 above consensus, and reported organic revenue growth of ~21% YoY—highest since 2022. Backlog grew to $8.10B; all segments expected to grow >mid-teens in H2. Street is 85% Buy with avg PT $405.91, and NTM P/E 38.2x vs 5-year avg 42.0x.

bullets.title: RCL Q2 beat; JPM/UBS raise FY26 EPS to $17.75-$17.87; 2H 'de-risked'
bullets.body: Royal Caribbean reported Q2 adj. EPS $4.21 (vs $3.97 consensus), net yield +1.2% cc (vs +0.2% guide) on strong close-in demand, and raised FY26 EPS guidance to $17.73-$17.87 from $17.10-$17.50. JPM maintains Overweight with $345 PT; UBS maintains Buy with PT under review. 2027 bookings pacing ahead of historic levels.

bullets.title: AAPL reclaims world's most valuable company from NVDA; stock at 52-week high (+57.8% YTD)
bullets.body: Apple reclaimed the title of world's most valuable company after 10 months, surpassing Nvidia. AAPL sits at $337.50, up 57.8% YTD and at a 52-week high. Separately, Zach AM Attack flags AAPL gross margin downside risk from memory cost inflation despite ~16% revenue growth from iPhone strength.

bullets.title: SMCI Taiwan offices raided in NVDA chip-smuggling probe; NVDA employee detained
bullets.body: Taiwan prosecutors raided Super Micro Computer's Taiwan offices as part of an investigation into alleged smuggling of NVDA chips to China. Separately, an NVDA employee was detained by Taiwan prosecutors in connection with the probe. Both events add to geopolitical/export-control headline risk for NVDA.

bullets.title: INTU downgraded to Hold at TD Cowen; target cut to $304 from $504
bullets.body: Intuit was downgraded to Hold from Buy at TD Cowen, with the price target slashed to $304 from $504—a 40% cut—reflecting valuation concerns in the broader software/AI momentum unwind.

bullets.title: SPOT: Citi hosting bull vs. bear debate July 31 amid margin timing questions
bullets.body: Spotify has underperformed since May's A-Day earnings, with investors debating the timing of new AI product rollouts and the trajectory of margin expansion. Citi is hosting a formal bull vs. bear debate on July 31 ahead of the next print.

bullets.title: ORCL and CRWV among 52-week lows; ORCL down 53% from high, CRWV down 7%+ today
bullets.body: ORCL hit a 52-week low at $114.80, down 53.2% from its 52-week high (down 4.3% intraday). CRWV is also at 52-week lows, down 7.1% on the Canadian exchange. Both neocloud names are down 21-28% since META's July 1 neocloud announcement, though MS argues compute scarcity provides pricing power.

bullets.title: CVNA: 22V flags bearish technical setup into earnings; avg post-earnings move >17%
bullets.body: 22V Research notes Carvana's technical profile has broken below long-term trend support, with a chart pattern resembling Tesla before its recent earnings decline. Historical post-earnings moves average >17% while current options imply a smaller move, suggesting the market is underpricing event risk.

bullets.title: DDOG: Citi raises PT to $300 from $270; 34% revenue growth seen as achievable
bullets.body: Citi raised its Datadog price target to $300 from $270 ahead of the print, citing 34% revenue growth as achievable and upside from AI-native customer demand. DDOG is up >80% YTD but analysts see further runway from both traditional and AI-native workloads.

bullets.title: TSLA: Multiple sources flag excessive 175x FY26 P/E; bear targets sub-$300
bullets.body: Multiple sources flag Tesla trading at over 175x FY26 P/E as AI-related multiples unwind more broadly. At least one analyst explicitly targets a decline below $300/share in the coming weeks, calling the valuation excessive relative to fundamentals and the broader multiple compression underway in AI-adjacent names.
